stem: Why does a program store data in a file rather than only in variables?

options.content: Data in a file is kept after the program ends
options.rationale: Correct: variables are lost when the program closes.

options.content: Files are faster to access than variables
options.rationale: Main memory is faster than secondary storage.

options.content: Variables cannot hold text data
options.rationale: STRING variables hold text.

options.content: Files make the program use less code
options.rationale: Using files adds statements; the benefit is permanence.

explanation: Files are on secondary storage, so the data survives after the program stops or the power goes off.

stem: Which statement opens the existing file `stock.txt` so that data can be taken from it?

options.content: `OPENFILE "stock.txt" FOR READ`
options.rationale: Correct: READ mode is for taking data from a file.

options.content: `OPENFILE "stock.txt" FOR WRITE`
options.rationale: WRITE creates a new file and loses the existing data.

options.content: `READFILE "stock.txt" FOR READ`
options.rationale: READFILE reads an item; it does not open the file.

options.content: `OPENFILE stock.txt READ`
options.rationale: The name needs quotes and the keyword FOR.

stem: Opening an existing file `FOR WRITE` keeps its data and adds new lines after it.
explanation: False. WRITE mode creates a new file; any data already in a file with that name is lost.

stem: After one `READFILE` statement, the next `READFILE` on the same open file reads the following line.
explanation: True. Each READFILE takes the next data item in order.

stem: Match each statement to what it does.

right.content: Adds the value as a new line in the file
Finishes using the file and releases it
Prepares an existing file so data can be read from it
Copies the next line of the file into a variable

explanation: Open, read or write, then close.

stem:
Complete the algorithm, which saves the 10 values of `Scores[1:10]` in `scores.txt`, one per line.

```
OPENFILE "scores.txt" FOR [1]
FOR Index ← 1 TO 10
    [2] "scores.txt", Scores[Index]
NEXT Index
[3] "scores.txt"
```
explanation: Open FOR WRITE, WRITEFILE each element, CLOSEFILE at the end.
hints: Open once before the loop and close once after it.

stem:
What does `names.txt` contain after this algorithm runs, if `Names[1:3]` holds Chipo, Farai and Rudo?

```
FOR Index ← 1 TO 3
    OPENFILE "names.txt" FOR WRITE
    WRITEFILE "names.txt", Names[Index]
    CLOSEFILE "names.txt"
NEXT Index
```

options.content: Chipo, Farai and Rudo on three lines
options.rationale: That needs the file opened once, before the loop.

options.content: Only Chipo
options.rationale: Later passes replace the file.

options.content: Nothing, because the file is closed
options.rationale: Closing saves the data that was written.

options.content: Only Rudo
options.rationale: Correct: each pass creates a new file, so only the last name remains.

explanation: Opening FOR WRITE starts an empty file every time. Open before the loop and close after it.
hints: What does WRITE mode do to a file each time it is opened?

stem:
The file `sales.txt` holds:

| Line | Contents of sales.txt |
|:-:|:-:|
| 1 | 125 |
| 2 | 98 |
| 3 | 143 |
| 4 | 110 |

```
Total ← 0
OPENFILE "sales.txt" FOR READ
FOR Day ← 1 TO 4
    READFILE "sales.txt", Amount
    Total ← Total + Amount
NEXT Day
CLOSEFILE "sales.txt"
OUTPUT Total
```

What is output?
workedSolution:
1. The four lines are read in order: 125, 98, 143, 110.
2. Total = 476.
hints: Each READFILE takes the next line.

stem:
The file `temps.txt` holds:

| Line | Contents of temps.txt |
|:-:|:-:|
| 1 | 28 |
| 2 | 33 |
| 3 | 31 |
| 4 | 26 |
| 5 | 35 |
| 6 | 30 |

```
OPENFILE "temps.txt" FOR READ
OPENFILE "hot.txt" FOR WRITE
FOR Day ← 1 TO 6
    READFILE "temps.txt", Reading
    IF Reading > 30
        THEN
            WRITEFILE "hot.txt", Reading
    ENDIF
NEXT Day
CLOSEFILE "temps.txt"
CLOSEFILE "hot.txt"
```

How many lines does `hot.txt` contain afterwards?
explanation: Readings over 30: 33, 31, 35: 3 lines. 30 itself is not greater than 30.
hints: Only values greater than 30 are written.

stem:
Why does this algorithm fail?

```
OPENFILE "log.txt" FOR WRITE
READFILE "log.txt", Entry
OUTPUT Entry
CLOSEFILE "log.txt"
```

options.content: CLOSEFILE must come before OUTPUT
options.rationale: The file can be closed after the output.

options.content: The file is opened for writing but then read
options.rationale: Correct: READFILE needs the file opened FOR READ.

options.content: Entry has not been declared as an array
options.rationale: A single variable receives one line.

options.content: File names cannot end in .txt
options.rationale: Any valid file name can be used.

explanation: Open FOR READ to read. (Opening FOR WRITE has also wiped the log.)

stem: Which pseudocode keyword is used to finish using a file once a program no longer needs it?
Which statement correctly writes the value of `Total` to the file `report.txt`, which is already open for writing?

options.content: `WRITEFILE Total, "report.txt"`
options.rationale: The file name comes first.

options.content: `OUTPUT "report.txt", Total`
options.rationale: OUTPUT displays on the screen; it does not write to a file.

options.content: `WRITEFILE "report.txt", Total`
options.rationale: Correct: file name in quotes, a comma, then the data.

options.content: `WRITEFILE report.txt, Total`
options.rationale: The file name is a string, so it needs quotes.

stem:
A game keeps its high score in `best.txt`.

```
OPENFILE "best.txt" FOR WRITE
READFILE "best.txt", Best
IF Score > Best
    THEN
        WRITEFILE "best.txt", Score
ENDIF
CLOSEFILE "best.txt"
```

What is the main logic problem?

options.content: Score and Best should both be strings
options.rationale: Numbers can be compared and written.

options.content: The IF statement needs an ELSE branch
options.rationale: No ELSE is required here.

options.content: The old high score is lost before it can be read
options.rationale: Correct: WRITE mode empties the file first.

options.content: CLOSEFILE should be inside the IF
options.rationale: The file must be closed whichever branch runs.

explanation: Open FOR READ, read Best, close; then, only if needed, open FOR WRITE and write the new score.
hints: What is in best.txt at the moment READFILE runs?

stem:
The file `club.txt` holds:

| Line | Contents of club.txt |
|:-:|:-:|
| 1 | Rudo |
| 2 | Sipho |
| 3 | Nyasha |
| 4 | END |
| 5 | Tendai |

```
Count ← 0
OPENFILE "club.txt" FOR READ
READFILE "club.txt", Member
WHILE Member <> "END" DO
    Count ← Count + 1
    READFILE "club.txt", Member
ENDWHILE
CLOSEFILE "club.txt"
OUTPUT Count
```

What is output?
explanation: Rudo, Sipho, Nyasha are counted; reading "END" stops the loop, so line 5 is never read. Output 3.
workedSolution:
1. Lines before END: Rudo, Sipho, Nyasha.
2. The terminator is not counted and the loop stops.
3. Count = 3.
hints: The loop stops when the line read is END.

stem: A school's library program stores its list of books in a file. Explain **two** reasons why.

points.description: The data is kept permanently / after the program closes or the computer is switched off, so it is available next time
The data can be shared with / used by another program or copied / backed up / prepared in advance without retyping

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The book list must still exist when the program is next run; in a file on secondary storage it is not lost when the program closes. The file can also be backed up or used by another program, such as one that prints reports.

hints: What happens to variables when the program closes?

stem: Write pseudocode that inputs 20 rainfall readings from the user and stores them in a new text file `rain.txt`, one reading per line.

points.description: Opens "rain.txt" FOR WRITE before the loop
Prompts and inputs a reading inside the loop
WRITEFILE "rain.txt" with the reading inside the loop

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: ```
DECLARE Reading : REAL
DECLARE Count : INTEGER
OPENFILE "rain.txt" FOR WRITE
FOR Count ← 1 TO 20
    OUTPUT "Enter rainfall reading ", Count
    INPUT Reading
    WRITEFILE "rain.txt", Reading
NEXT Count
CLOSEFILE "rain.txt"
```

explanation: Open, loop with input and write, close.
hints: Open once, loop 20 times, close once.

stem:
A shop in Masvingo stores its products in `products.txt`: each product name is followed on the next line by its price.

| Line | Contents of products.txt |
|:-:|:-:|
| 1 | Soap |
| 2 | 1.50 |
| 3 | Rice |
| 4 | 4.25 |
| 5 | Salt |
| 6 | 0.80 |

```
OPENFILE "products.txt" FOR READ
FOR Item ← 1 TO 3
    READFILE "products.txt", ProductName[Item]
    READFILE "products.txt", Price[Item]
NEXT Item
CLOSEFILE "products.txt"
```

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State the value of `ProductName[2]` after the algorithm runs.

parts.label: (b)
parts.workedSolution:
1. Pass 3 reads lines 5 and 6.
2. Line 6 is the price of Salt: 0.8.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Why must the loop run exactly 3 times?

options.content: A FOR loop that reads a file can only run 3 times
options.rationale: There is no such limit.

options.content: The file holds exactly 3 products and has no end marker
options.rationale: Correct: reading more lines than exist would fail.

options.content: Each READFILE statement reads three lines
options.rationale: Each READFILE reads one line.

options.content: The arrays can only hold 3 characters
options.rationale: The arrays hold whole names and prices.

parts.explanation: The number of records must be known (or a terminator used).

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Write pseudocode that writes the name of every product costing more than 1.00 to a new file `dear.txt`, using the arrays filled above.

points.description: Opens "dear.txt" FOR WRITE before the loop and closes it after

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: ```
OPENFILE "dear.txt" FOR WRITE
FOR Item ← 1 TO 3
    IF Price[Item] > 1.00
        THEN
            WRITEFILE "dear.txt", ProductName[Item]
    ENDIF
NEXT Item
CLOSEFILE "dear.txt"
```

explanation: ProductName[2] = Rice; Price[3] = 0.8; the dearest product is Rice.
hints: Lines alternate: a name, then its price.
Each pass of the loop reads two lines.

stem:
A museum in Harare keeps a visitor log in `log.txt`, one line per day. The file currently holds 3 lines:

| Line | Contents of log.txt |
|:-:|:-:|
| 1 | Mon 14 |
| 2 | Tue 22 |
| 3 | Wed 17 |

The programmer wants to add today's line, `"Thu 19"`, and writes:

```
OPENFILE "log.txt" FOR WRITE
WRITEFILE "log.txt", "Thu 19"
CLOSEFILE "log.txt"
```

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: How many lines does `log.txt` contain after this runs?
parts.explanation: WRITE mode creates a new file, so only the new line remains.
parts.workedSolution:
1. OPENFILE FOR WRITE empties the file.
2. One WRITEFILE: 1 line.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The lines for Mon, Tue and Wed are still in the file.
parts.explanation: False. They were lost when the file was opened FOR WRITE.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Write pseudocode that adds the new line correctly. It should read the 3 existing lines into an array `Days[1:4]`, store the new line as the 4th element and write all 4 lines back to `log.txt`.

points.description: Opens "log.txt" FOR WRITE and loops 1 to 4 with WRITEFILE "log.txt", Days[Index]

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: ```
DECLARE Days : ARRAY[1:4] OF STRING
DECLARE Index : INTEGER
OPENFILE "log.txt" FOR READ
FOR Index ← 1 TO 3
    READFILE "log.txt", Days[Index]
NEXT Index
CLOSEFILE "log.txt"
Days[4] ← "Thu 19"
OPENFILE "log.txt" FOR WRITE
FOR Index ← 1 TO 4
    WRITEFILE "log.txt", Days[Index]
NEXT Index
CLOSEFILE "log.txt"
```

explanation: Only 1 line remains, because WRITE mode starts a new file. Read the old lines first, then write them all back with the new one.
hints: Copy the old lines into an array first, or write to a second file.
